text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Almost half of Portugal's active population of 4.25 million people have "precarious" jobs, according to a study.
- Portuguese public sector debt has fallen every year since 1992. A source in the Finance Ministry said the budget deficit would stand at 4.0 and 2.9 percent in 1996 and 1997 respectively.
- Most Portuguese are willing to make sacrifices in order to qualify for entry to the euro, a poll by Euroteste shows.
- Spain is angry with Portugal over the denial of the extradition of ETA suspect Jose Luis Telletxea Maya by the Portuguese Supreme Court.

* Negotiations between Saudi Aramco and Petrogal at an impasse, a source involved in the talks told the paper. Saudi Aramco wants to take a direct stake in Petrogal, but private shareholders' unit Petrocontrol would like to conduct the negotiations.
* President Jorge Sampaio, speaking after an eight-day visit to China, said he was optimistic about prospects for the development of the country.
